approval.rationale: A continuous, fine-grained dark rock face with small vesicles and pale specks and no joints or slabs; its only features are two small stains near the corners. Cooked with a narrower de-light (1/16), a 0.3 wrap band and chroma evening the tiling is even at the 2 m scale, so the crags' 11-30 m faces read as one rock; gain 1.7 lifts its linear mean from 0.053 to about 0.09, because at the candidate's own value the crags went near-black in game and lost their facets.
limitations: Reads as dark vesicular basalt rather than granite: still darker than the granite talus and boulders beside it (linear mean about 0.09 against 0.16).
Uniform at every scale: no strata, joints, streaks or lichen; large-scale variation comes only from the crag's facets, baked AO and the snow or moss.
The wide wrap band and stronger de-light soften the grain near the tile edges; two faint stains still repeat every 2 m.
